children: The bank will issue 50,000 listed, unsecured and subordinated NCDs with a face value of Rs 1 lakh each through private placement

Shares of Equitas Small Finance Bank (SFB) gained during trading on Wednesday, 16 September, after the bank’s board approved raising up to Rs 500 crore through the issuance of non-convertible debentures (NCDs).

According to a regulatory filing, the board at its meeting on 16 September approved the issuance of 50,000 rated, listed, unsecured, subordinated, transferable, redeemable and fully paid-up lower Tier II NCDs.

The NCDs, with a face value of Rs 1 lakh each and an aggregate nominal value of up to Rs 500 crore, will be issued in a single series in dematerialised form on a private placement basis. The NCDs are proposed to be listed on the BSE.

Equitas SFB reported a net profit of Rs 184 crore for the April-June quarter of the 2026-27 financial year (Q1 FY27), compared with a loss of Rs 224 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. The bank had reported a profit of Rs 213 crore in the preceding quarter.
Its net interest income (NII) stood at Rs 1,029 crore during Q1 FY27, up 30.9 per cent year-on-year from Rs 786 crore in Q1 FY26.

The bank’s gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declined to 2.36 per cent in Q1 FY27 from 2.49 per cent in the preceding quarter. However, net non-performing assets (NNPA) increased to 0.70 per cent from 0.68 per cent in Q4 FY26.

Equitas SFB shares rose nearly 2 per cent to an intraday high of Rs 72.69 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Wednesday, compared with the previous close of Rs 71.35. At around 2:22 pm, the stock was trading 1.18 per cent higher at Rs 72.19.
The stock has declined nearly 1 per cent over the past week and 3 per cent over the past month. On a year-to-date basis, it has gained 13 per cent.
The shares touched a 52-week high of Rs 83.90 on 15 July 2026 and a 52-week low of Rs 51.25 on 30 March 2026.
Equitas Small Finance Bank had a market capitalisation of Rs 8,259.19 crore as of 16 September 2026, according to NSE data.
